mainEntity.name: What Is the Difference Between a Cobot Palletizer and a Traditional Robotic Palletizer?

acceptedAnswer.text: A cobot palletizer uses a collaborative robot, an arm designed for shared workspaces and moderate speeds, in a compact standardized cell. A traditional robotic palletizer uses an industrial robot with higher speed, payload and duty cycle. TRFCobot is the collaborative option for lower-speed, high-mix lines, while TRFCompact and TRFSpeed use industrial robots for higher rates and heavier cases.

mainEntity.name: How Many Cases per Minute Can a Robotic Palletizer Handle?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the platform. TRFCobot covers about 1 to 10 cases per minute, TRFCompact about 5 to 15 and TRFSpeed about 10 to 35. These are typical ranges for commercial screening: TRF confirms the final rate for your product, end-of-arm tool, pallet pattern and reach, and applications above that range move to a custom palletizer.

mainEntity.name: What Payload Does a Palletizing Robot Need for My Product?

acceptedAnswer.text: The robot must carry the heaviest unit plus the end-of-arm tool, and for multi-case picks, the combined weight of the cases. TRFCobot handles cases up to about 22 lb, TRFCompact up to about 44 lb and TRFSpeed up to about 66 lb. TRF validates the final payload with your product, gripper, pallet pattern and reach.

mainEntity.name: Can a Robotic Palletizer Operate Below Freezing (32°F)?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, with equipment built for that environment. TRFSubzero is the TRF palletizer for areas below 32°F, used in frozen food, ice cream, frozen prepared foods and meat processing in below-freezing areas. The Custom Foods case study shows palletizing below freezing in a published installation.

mainEntity.name: How Does a Robotic Palletizer Handle SKU or Pallet Pattern Changeovers?

acceptedAnswer.text: Pallet patterns are stored as recipes, so an SKU change usually means selecting the recipe that holds the case data, pick logic and pattern for the new product. When the new unit fits the same end-of-arm tool, the change happens mostly in software; otherwise the cell needs a tool change. TRF reviews your full SKU and pattern list before recommending a platform.

mainEntity.name: Can a Palletizer Be Integrated With My Existing Conveyor and Wrapping Line?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. The palletizer needs cases in the right orientation, at a steady rhythm and with enough accumulation upstream to absorb a pallet change. TRFIntraflow provides conveying, accumulation and routing modules with palletizer interfaces. End-of-line integration puts case packing, conveying, palletizing and the wrapping, labeling and warehouse interfaces under one engineering scope, and interfaces with equipment you already own are defined during project engineering.

mainEntity.name: How Much Does a Robotic Palletizer Cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: Reference list prices are US$ 120,000 for the TRFCobot Dual, US$ 180,000 for the TRFCompact Dual and US$ 350,000 for the TRFSpeed 100, all EX Works Lenexa, Kansas, installation not included. Installation, line integration and options are quoted with your application. The robotic palletizer cost guide explains each cost driver.

mainEntity.name: What Is the Typical Payback Period for a Robotic Palletizer?

acceptedAnswer.text: Payback depends on the labor hours the palletizer replaces, shifts per day, local labor cost and the cost of the system. The estimate takes the total system cost, including maintenance, and divides it by the annual labor cost of manual palletizing minus the electricity the robot uses, using reference production wages by state. The palletizing ROI calculator returns an initial estimate that a TRF Sales Engineer completes with your project costs.
